title: ‘Am I Supposed to be a Comedian?’: Donald Trump’s Bizarre White House Correspondent’s Dinner Speech Had Few Laughing
description: Even by the standards to which we’ve all, by now, become accustomed, President Donald Trump’s performance at Friday night’s White House Corresponden
body:
Even by the standards to which we’ve all, by now, become accustomed, President Donald Trump’s performance at Friday night’s White House Correspondents’ Dinner was bizarre. And the fact of it — from the style of his halting delivery to the substance of his vindictive message to a journalists’ group who’d handed him a mic — made clear that he’s now in something of a spiral. A public figure who, more than any politician or celebrity in our history, has placed the desire for approval at the center of his brand is being confronted by his dwindling popularity. (His approval rating was one of the topics Trump touched upon in a speech that felt less like what he calls “the weave” than like a ramble.) He doesn’t like that his style is falling out of favor, and he’s going to make sure, for the next two-plus years or perhaps even longer, that we know he doesn’t.
	

	Trump’s speech Friday night served as a re-do of the planned address he was meant to give at the original 2026 WHCD in April, which was marred by a gunman firing shots inside the Washington Hilton. He had promised, then, to excoriate the press; on a rescheduled and more somber evening months later, he seemed unsure, at first, how to act. “Let’s have a little bit of fun,” he said. “What do we do here? Is this supposed to be fun, am I supposed to be serious, am I supposed to be a comedian?” But old reflexes kicked in: Just before this, Trump had complained about the evening’s awards, which had gone to various journalists whose work (naturally, given their profession covering the current administration) had been adversarial to his interests. “This has not been an easy evening, all those awards,” he said. “Do I have a say?” Later, he’d go on to criticize journalists including CNN’s Kaitlan Collins and the Wall Street Journal’s Josh Dawsey by name. 
	

	It’s an article of faith among the online #Resistance that Trump’s never having won an Emmy for “The Apprentice” is a crucial part of his origin story; just because an insight has been dulled by repetition, though, doesn’t make it untrue. The White House Correspondents’ Dinner is an evening of entertainment programming and an awards ceremony. The latter thing seems to activate something primal within Trump; the former presents for him an opportunity to redefine reality along his own terms, and to force an increasingly bored and quiet audience along for the ride. (Indeed, during his speech, Trump recollected the 2011 Correspondents’ Dinner, at which then-President Barack Obama brutally roasted him, as a fun evening he enjoyed, especially because it felt good to be at the center of attention. That is not how the event is widely remembered!)

	There was an air of flop sweat to the evening: Like any inept emcee, Trump began blaming unnamed joke writers for basic material — light, sub-Friars Club material lovingly roasting his allies Nicki Minaj and Bari Weiss — falling flat, but his own delivery seemed oddly nervous. In the past, Trump has dominated journalists. Indeed, he’d told the world that’s what he planned to do at April’s first version of this event. Instead, though, Trump seemed affronted and almost frightened of the crowd before him when discussing his own popularity, and diminished as he ran through tired material: The Oscars’ decline in ratings over time, for instance, or his antipathy to Chris Christie, Bruce Springsteen and Jane Fonda. 

	Once, Trump’s raging against the Oscars had a certain charge to it. That’s not because his claims that the show’s ratings are down because of how liberal celebrities are (there’s a lot more to it than that), but because, as a seeming vanguard of seismic cultural change, Trump had the power to subsume basically any entity. Now, though, it’s just sadly predictable. This man has been the defining element of American politics for ten years. We know that he cares a lot about awards! We don’t need to be told again!

	That, more than sorrow over the American President going after journalists or mild bemusement that he couldn’t land a Borscht belt joke about an aging Senator unable to consummate his marriage any longer, feels like the takeaway from a vexed, pointless hour of speech. The strange and at-times unknowable mind that even recently gave us turns of phrase like “the late, great Hannibal Lecter” is now hung up on a public that, faced with inflation and an unpopular war in Iran, isn’t laughing anymore. And that mind’s response is to return to safe and comfortable territory, re-fighting old battles with Rosie O’Donnell and with various awards-giving bodies. The show has lost even what lurid appeal it might have held for Trump’s morbidly curious critics. And yet it will go on, and on. Trump vowed, jokingly-but-not, to run for re-election (which the Constitution bars) in 2028. And yet listening to his deflated delivery, one could tell that his heart wasn’t in it. Perhaps he was thinking about who’d won the awards earlier that night.

schema.headline: ‘Am I Supposed to be a Comedian?’: Donald Trump’s Bizarre White House Correspondent’s Dinner Speech Had Few Laughing

title: ‘The Odyssey’ Leaked on X: High-Quality Bootleg Seen by Millions in Hours Before Takedown
description:
“The Odyssey” leaks have begun, as a high-quality bootleg of the film reached millions of people on X thanks to a viral tweet on July 25.

	At 2:25
body:
“The Odyssey” leaks have begun, as a high-quality bootleg of the film reached millions of people on X thanks to a viral tweet on July 25.

	At 2:25 p.m. PT, a post on X reading “Someone uploaded ‘The Odyssey’ full movie on X. Can you believe it?” amplified a message from a now-suspended account. The message included a high-quality version of the film, as confirmed by Variety, and climbed to over 2.1 million views within two and a half hours. By that time, the streaming film was replaced by a takedown notice, and then the account was suspended.
	

	It certainly doesn’t seem to have hurt the film’s still-surging box office in its second weekend, during which it earned another $87 million, or lessen demand for the coveted Imax 70 mm tickets.


	As of July 26, a few clones of the bootlegged film are available on X, but they’ve been mostly flooded away by mislabeled files promising “The Odyssey” but actually showing a Rickroll, the longtime internet prank of tricking people into watching the music video for Rick Astley’s 1987 song “Never Gonna Give You Up.”

	Beyond piracy, X owner Elon Musk has been vocal with his opinions on the Christopher Nolan movie, insulting casting choices in particular, writing, “Who specifically is the asshole who added DEI lies to Academy Awards eligibility instead of it just being about making the best movie?” Musk then said his AI tool Grok Imagine would make a “historically accurate” version of the film to release this year.

schema.headline: ‘The Odyssey’ Leaked on X: High-Quality Bootleg Seen by Millions in Hours Before Takedown

title: ‘Rick and Morty’ Spinoff ‘President Curtis’ Plays It Safe, but Keeps the Sci-Fi Franchise Cruising: TV Review
description: “They spin off so fast,” Morty (Harry Belden) sighs of the latest visitors to the garage he shares with his grandfather Rick (Ian Cardoni). “I give
body:
“They spin off so fast,” Morty (Harry Belden) sighs of the latest visitors to the garage he shares with his grandfather Rick (Ian Cardoni). “I give it 10 episodes,” Rick replies.

	The scene is an obligatory, efficient passing of the baton from the characters’ namesake show “Rick and Morty,” a juggernaut hit for Adult Swim now in its 13th year and ninth season, to its inaugural satellite. But the shared DNA is already evident. “President Curtis,” co-created by “Rick and Morty” collaborators Dan Harmon (also well-known for the cult hit sitcom “Community”) and James Siciliano, is another animated procedural that blends high concept science fiction with proudly juvenile — yet consistently sharp — humor. Keith David’s titular commander-in-chief is a recurring character on the flagship show, and there’s visual continuity between the two series’ dense jumble of 2D sight gags. “President Curtis” nonetheless announces itself as a spiritual sibling to “Rick and Morty” more in sensibility than canonical connections, to fans’ likely satisfaction.
	

	“President Curtis” opens with a press conference in which our nation’s leader declares that “I killed Paul Bunyan today,” with David adding in his sonorous baritone: “Timber, bitch!” (A veteran voice actor, David has long had a gift for leveraging the assumed seriousness of his natural timbre for comedy. The same skill is utilized in live action on the FX crime series “The Lowdown,” among other projects.) The gag is an early indication of a slight preference for the supernatural over the aliens and interdimensional creatures of “Rick and Morty,” though rest assured our protagonists do make the occasional trip to space. They just also interface with vampires, witches and werewolves on a regular basis, as one does when attempting to lead the free world. “We don’t tattle,” one character lectures another. “We’re grown-ups — we fight ninjas!”
	

	Curtis’ trusty aides-de-camp in this enterprise are his new chief of staff Banks (Stephanie Beatriz), a cyborg given to overriding her own self-imposed ethics protocols, and Special Agent O’Doyle (“Community” alum Jim Rash), a Secret Service member who also happens to be half leprechaun. Every episode, the trio confront a new threat that has nothing to do with bo-ring agenda items like reducing the deficit, from investigating escapes at a “paranormal Guantanamo” to locating Napoleon’s mummified penis so France can’t undo the Louisiana Purchase. (Just roll with it.) The chair of Curtis’ unidentified political party may complain that her organization “doesn’t care about you kicking Mothman into high-voltage fencing” while inquiring after an infrastructure bill, but both the show’s priorities and ours are the inverse.

	Inventive and breathlessly paced, “President Curtis” brings the “Rick and Morty” ethos quite literally back to Earth, where there’s less head-spinning, stakes-nullifying multiverse material. We’re mostly dealing with one version of Curtis, Banks and O’Doyle, which proves more than enough given all they have on their plate — like keeping the CIA from learning the truth about the moon landing. (The Curtis administration is the stuff of conspiracy theorists’ fantasies or nightmares, depending on one’s point of view.) But “President Curtis” also starts in the place “Rick and Morty” came to only gradually, after the early seasons pursued a more serialized story about Rick, an arrogant absentee father whose only sacred ideal is his own genius, reconnecting with his family. 

	Over time, “Rick and Morty” largely abandoned, or at least became much more sporadic with, thematic heft and canon-advancing events as its focus turned to sustainable longevity. From the start, however, “President Curtis” is relatively light on emotional stakes. Curtis is divorced, and still carries a torch for his ex-wife (Kelsey Scott) — now the governor of Illinois and architect of an innovative monster rehabilitation program with the Candyman (as in the movies) its star participant. But the president’s love life is deployed more as a background character detail than a driving force of the overall story.
	

	Instead, “President Curtis” is more comfortable as a vehicle for game guest stars (like Kristen Schaal as a seemingly immortal Amelia Earhart), pop culture allusions (Anne Rice and Us Weekly enter the lexicon) and whatever elaborate bits the writers can come up with. The main cast and the domestic focus may be new compared to “Rick and Morty,” but the general feeling is the same. This means “President Curtis” delivers more on dependability than strict innovation, though that may be what both viewers and a parent corporation looking to beef up its IP reserves on the cusp of a potential merger want. Rick Sanchez is a kid’s fantasy of a zany, indulgent grandpa; President Curtis self-describes as “America’s cool dad.” It doesn’t take a Rick-level genius to see the parallels.

	“President Curtis” will premiere on Adult Swim on July 26 at 11:30 p.m. ET, with remaining episodes airing weekly on Sundays and available to stream on HBO Max the next day.

title: Box Office: ‘Toy Story 5’ Crosses $1 Billion, Becomes Highest-Grossing Movie of the Year
description: Who says toys are outdated? Disney and Pixar’s “Toy Story 5,” which grapples with the reality that kids would rather play with tech than dolls, has
body:
Who says toys are outdated? Disney and Pixar’s “Toy Story 5,” which grapples with the reality that kids would rather play with tech than dolls, has surpassed $1 billion globally and now ranks as the highest-grossing release of the year.

	The film has earned $448 million domestically and $573 million internationally for a global tally of $1.022 billion. It’s the third movie of the year to cross the coveted milestone, following “The Super Mario Galaxy Movie” ($1.001 billion) and “Michael” ($1.001 billion). Meanwhile, “The Odyssey,” which has earned $639.6 million after just two weekends of release, is primed to be the fourth film to notch $1 billion. And that’s before “Spider-Man: Brand New Day,” a sequel to 2021’s juggernaut “No Way Home,” opens on July 31.
	

	This year is tracking to produce the most billion-dollar blockbusters since the pandemic upended the box office in 2020. In 2019, nine movies — including “Avengers: Endgame,” “The Lion King,” “Aladdin,” “Joker,” “Spider-Man: Far From Home” and “Captain Marvel” — earned over $1 billion. The following year, plagued with months of COVID-related theater closures, not a single film crossed the billion-dollar mark. There was just one in 2021 (“Spider-Man: No Way Home”), three in 2022 (“Avatar: The Way of Water,” “Top Gun: Maverick” and “Jurassic World Dominion”), two in 2023 (“Barbie” and “The Super Mario Bros. Movie”), three in 2024 (“Inside Out 2,” “Deadpool & Wolverine” and “Moana 2″) and three in 2025 (“Zootopia 2,” “Avatar: Fire and Ash” and “Lilo & Stitch”).
	

	In the coming days, “Toy Story 5″ will register as the highest-grossing installment in the beloved franchise, overtaking 2019’s “Toy Story 4″ ($1.07 billion). It’s the third “Toy Story” sequel to cross $1 billion after 2010’s “Toy Story 3″ ($1.06 billion).

	Directed by Pixar veteran Andrew Stanton, the fifth installment follows Woody (Tom Hanks), Buzz Lightyear (Tim Allen), Jessie (Joan Cusack) and the gang of anthropomorphic toys as their owner Bonnie becomes addicted to her new favorite gadget, a kiddie smart tablet known as Lilypad. “Toy Story 5″ opened in mid-June to $160 million, marking the biggest debut of the year as well as the best start in the series. With glowing reviews, positive word-of-mouth and general goodwill toward the 31-year-old property, “Toy Story 5″ remained the de facto choice for family audiences through the busy summer season. It didn’t hurt that Taylor Swift, whose wedding to Travis Kelce was among the buzziest news of the summer, wrote a new song, “I Knew It, I Knew You,” for the soundtrack.

	Amid the outsized success of “Toy Story 5,” Pixar Animation Studios was hit last week by layoffs at Disney. Although animated sequels have majorly rebounded at the box office, original fare remains challenged. Pixar’s other 2026 release was this spring’s new adventure “Hoppers,” the story of an animal-loving student who transfers her mind into a robotic beaver so she can talk to other critters. Despite a strong opening weekend, “Hoppers” didn’t have the staying power to match the box office heights of prior Pixar greats.

schema.headline: Box Office: ‘Toy Story 5’ Crosses $1 Billion, Becomes Highest-Grossing Movie of the Year

title: Inside ‘Colony’: ‘Train to Busan’ Director Yeon Sang-ho and Gianna Jun Discuss Their Thrilling New Take on the Zombie Movie
description:
“Train to Busan” proved that humans can’t outrun the infected. “Colony” proves they can’t outsmart them. 

	Director Yeon Sang-ho returns to the zom
body:
“Train to Busan” proved that humans can’t outrun the infected. “Colony” proves they can’t outsmart them. 

	Director Yeon Sang-ho returns to the zombie genre with his third live-action thriller, “Colony,” expanding the “Yeoniverse,” the cinematic universe he’s built through his genre-defining horror films. The South Korean film marks Gianna Jun’s (aka Jun Ji-hyun) long-awaited return to the big screen after 11 years alongside Koo Kyo-hwan and Ji Chang-wook. 
	

	“Colony,” which made its North American premiere as the opening night film of the 25th New York Asian Film Festival, and will arrive in U.S. theaters August 28 through Well Go USA, follows Kwon Se-jeong, played by Gianna, an unemployed biotech professor who becomes trapped inside a high-rise building after a rapidly mutating virus breaks out. The survivors must escape while the infected evolve into something smarter and more dangerous than you’re run-of-the-mill zombies.


	Indeed, the zombies in “Colony” are unlike anything audiences have seen from Yeon before. Rather than standard reanimated corpses, the infected are connected by a collective intelligence, allowing them to learn, adapt and coordinate as one. When one zombie evolves, the entire group evolves with it. 



	

					Yeon Sang-ho and Gianna Jun attend the 2026 New York Asian Film Festival opening night premiere of “Colony” at Walter Reade Theater on July 10, 2026, in New York City.
									Getty Images
	



	“The hardest part,” Yeon explains to Variety, “was figuring out how to visually express zombies that exist in the form of a colony with collective intelligence. To convey that intuitively to the audience, the movement of the zombies had to be unique.” In “Train to Busan,” he used breakdancers to choreograph the infected’s movements. “Colony” took a different approach: “This time, we hired modern dance teams who were more experienced in choreographing group movements in an effort to create movements that could place a stronger emphasis on their collective nature.” 
	

	According to Yeon, the idea of a collective organism influenced his approach to the film. “I found it very interesting how, in reality, actual collective or colony-based organisms always produce variants or mutations. The reason for this is that because they are a group made of the exact same properties, if a single weakness is discovered, the entire colony could die off all at once, so they constantly create variants.”

	The driving force behind the film’s antagonist, Seo Young-chul (Koo Kyo-hwan), is his belief that imperfect communication is the source of all tragedy. This belief causes him to orchestrate the film’s bioterrorist attack. Yeon, however, doesn’t agree with him. 

	“I think I’ve explored the question of what it means to be ‘human’ through many of my previous films,” he maintains. “In this work, I had the same concerns. What I consider to be ‘humanism’ in this film is individuality. In other words, I believe that humans have no choice but to possess individuality, and because we can’t achieve perfect communication, we are actually all the more human.”



	While Young-chul sees individuality as humanity’s greatest flaw, Se-jeong’s character represents the strength of it. While developing Se-jeong, Yeon envisioned a character who was an outcast but not someone weakened by isolation. He wanted her to be someone who is assertive and confident enough to choose solitude for herself. “Kwon Se-jeong is a complex character. She has to be someone who is an outcast but also someone who is confident,” he says. “When I thought about who could express that, I naturally thought of Gianna.” 

	Yeon’s admiration for Gianna’s ability to portray unconventional female characters goes back to the beginning of her career. “Even in her debut film, ‘My Sassy Girl,’ her character was something that had never really been seen before in Korean cinema,” he offers. “I’ve always thought of her as an actress who shifted the paradigm for female characters. Since then, she has continued to shift that paradigm multiple times through various roles and performances.”

	The film’s ending scene hints that the battle against the infected may not be over. Yeon admits there are already plans for what comes next but not in the way fans expect. Rather than teasing another film, Yeon revealed that he is currently discussing the possibility of continuing the story of “Colony” as a video game with Smilegate, the film’s co-producer and game developer. 
	



	

					A scene from “Colony.”
									Well Go USA
	



	As far as the inspirations behind “Colony” go, Yeon pointed to the 1978 sci-fi horror classic “Invasion of the Body Snatchers” as one of the biggest influences behind the film. Other recent works that inspired him were “28 Years Later” and “The Last of Us.” 

	As Korean cinema continues to expand globally, Gianna was asked whether she hopes to pursue any Hollywood projects in the future. The short answer is no. “I strongly feel that ‘what is most Korean is what is most global,’” she says. “Rather than seeking out work abroad, I think it’s more meaningful to work with great directors and actors right here in Korea.”

	Yeon shared a similar sentiment when asked about a potential Hollywood remake of “Train to Busan.” While acknowledging that there had been some efforts to remake the film in English, he said he has no desire to direct one himself: “I feel I’ve fully expressed everything I wanted to do through the original film ‘Train to Busan.’” 

	Nearly a decade after “Train to Busan” changed the perception of Korean horror worldwide, “Colony” suggests that the next evolution of onscreen zombies isn’t one that is simply faster or stronger, but one that is smarter.

schema.headline: Inside ‘Colony’: ‘Train to Busan’ Director Yeon Sang-ho and Gianna Jun Discuss Their Thrilling New Take on the Zombie Movie

title: Marvel’s Comic-Con Panel Excites Fans for ‘Doomsday’ but Leaves Them Cautiously Optimistic About What’s Beyond
description: Diehard Marvel fans packed into San Diego Comic Con’s massive Hall H Saturday night, some even camping out for more than 30 hours. But as the 40-min
body:
Diehard Marvel fans packed into San Diego Comic Con’s massive Hall H Saturday night, some even camping out for more than 30 hours. But as the 40-minute panel wrapped up with just two surprise announcements — a Ghost Rider movie starring Ryan Gosling and “Black Panther 3” — it’s hard not to feel like, “Is that it?”

	After a 30-minute delay, the panel got underway with Marvel Studios chief Kevin Feige acknowledging writer and producer Stephen Wacker’s new role as Marvel Comics editor-in-chief. He then rolled out a trailer for the “Avengers: Endgame” re-release, dubbed “Endgame Encore,” which will have an exclusive sneak peek at “Doomsday.” But fans were hungry for new announcements, not a re-edited trailer for a movie they’ve likely seen multiple times (and no doubt will see again).
	

	Gosling and director Shawn Levy re-teaming for a Ghost Rider movie was a surprise, albeit one that the actor has been attracted to for years. The announcement capped off an extended bit with “Happy Sad Confused” host Josh Horowitz, who recalled all the times he’s asked Gosling about the long-rumored movie in interviews. Unless fans have been glued to every MCU rumor, Gosling’s introduction from Horowitz didn’t track well on stage. After Marvel’s “Blade” movie never fully materialized, it’s hard not to take an “I’ll believe it when I see it” stance on the “Ghost Rider” — despite the fact that “Deadpool and Wolverine” director Shawn Levy is already locked in. 


	The other awkward moment from Marvel’s panel came during an confusing Deadpool cameo. As the sprawling “Doomsday” cast joined the stage, a very recognizable voice called out from the sea of fans. Deadpool, clad in his gray X-Force costume, appeared in the crowd — but never removed his mask to show who was underneath. It certainly sounded like Ryan Reynolds begging for a role in the movie, but it wasn’t clear if Reynolds himself was in the suit. Joe and Anthony Russo joked that production had wrapped on “Doomsday” but then…that was it. While it’s been highly speculated that Deadpool may cameo in both “Doomsday” and 2027’s “Secret Wars,” Feige skipped the opportunity to confirm Reynolds’ return to the MCU.
	

	Instead, Feige and the Russos moved straight into showing an exclusive trailer for “Doomsday,” which featured more backstory for Downey’s villain, but also some recycled footage from the last teaser. We learn more about Doom’s complicated history with the Fantastic Four and his seemingly tortured past, but much of the plot is still shrouded. The most exciting moment came when Doom resurrected a fleet of giant Sentinel robots — robotic villains from the “X-Men” universe — to battle the heroes.

	The panel ended with another long-rumored announcement, Ryan Coogler’s “Black Panther 3,” but with a major surprise: “Alien: Romulus” actor David Jonsson is taking over the title role. He’ll play T’Challa II, the son of the late Chadwick Boseman’s hero, in what will no doubt be another emotional film for Coogler and the Wakanda crew. Jonsson is an exciting young actor on the rise and was excellent in last year’s adaptation of Stephen King’s “The Long Walk.” It will be impossible to fill Boseman’s shoes, but Jonsson stands to be one of the major pieces in the next era of Marvel.

	So far, “Ghost Rider” and “Black Panther 3,” both slated for 2028, are the only movies in Marvel’s next phase after “Doomsday” and “Secret Wars.” Fans have long expected — and Feige has stated that — the X-Men to help steer the MCU’s future, but there wasn’t a single X-announcement on stage Saturday. Several of Fox’s “X-Men” stars are returning for “Doomsday,” but there was no indication if they’ll be back for “Secret Wars” or beyond. Rumors about the next cast of X-Men have swirled online, but at the panel, all the focus was on “Doomsday” — not whatever may come next.

	Maybe expectations were set too high. Last time Marvel attended Comic Con was in 2024, when the studio made the bombshell reveal that Robert Downey Jr., the actor who carried the MCU on his back for over a decade, would return as its next major villain: Doctor Doom. That announcement nearly blew the roof off of Hall H, but nothing matched that intensity this year. Seeing the crowd of fans dressed in Doom costumes was fun for a few seconds, but watching everyone crowd together for a selfie — and not getting more information on “Doomsday” — was not.

	Luckily, Disney has its D23 event in just three weeks, where more news will surely come. However, Comic-Con has usually been a film-centric event, where D23 has more TV shows. Everyone expects “Doomsday” to be a much-needed hit for the MCU later this year, but can it ascend to the two billion-dollar heights of “Endgame”? And how will it fare against Warner Bros.’ “Dune: Part 3,” which is hitting theaters the same day on Dec. 18? As the “Dunesday” showdown approaches, Marvel needs every bit of hype it can get to pave the way for its future, and Comic-Con could’ve used a few more major announcements to cement it as a must-see cultural event.

schema.headline: Marvel’s Comic-Con Panel Excites Fans for ‘Doomsday’ but Leaves Them Cautiously Optimistic About What’s Beyond

title: ‘Black Panther 3’: David Jonsson to Play T’Challa’s Son as December 2028 Release Date Set
description:
Black Panther is back!

	David Jonsson has been cast as the new Black Panther and is playing T’Challa’s son in “Black Panther 3,”  out Dec. 15, 2028
body:
Black Panther is back!

	David Jonsson has been cast as the new Black Panther and is playing T’Challa’s son in “Black Panther 3,”  out Dec. 15, 2028. The film will follow Jonsson’s character, Prince T’Challa II, as he comes of age after he was introduced as a child in “Black Panther: Wakanda Forever.”

	Director Ryan Coogler will return for the third film, as well as Leticia Wright reprising her role as Shuri and Winston Duke as M’Baku. The news was announced at Marvel’s Comic-Con Hall H panel. 
	

	Wright took over as Black Panther from her late co-star Chadwick Boseman in “Black Panther: Wakanda Forever,” with Shuri becoming the eponymous superhero. Boseman, who portrayed T’Challa in the first “Black Panther,” died of colon cancerat age 43 in 2020, when Coogler was working on the sequel. The character T’Challa II was introduced as T’Challa and Nakia’s (Lupita Nyong’o) son in “Wakanda Forever.” 


	Jonsson recently starred in “Alien Romulus” and the adaptation of Stephen King’s “The Long Walk.” Wright told Variety in January 2023 after the release of “Wakanda Forever” that she thought the third film in the franchise was “already in the works.”

	“You know, we just had a terrific two years of bringing it out and everybody coming together to support it,” Wright said in the interview. “We need a little bit of a break, we need to regroup and Ryan needs to get back into the lab, so it’s going to take a little while, but we’re really excited for you guys to see that.”

	The first “Black Panther” movie, released in 2018, took in $1.3 billion at the worldwide box office, and starred Boseman, Wright, Lupita Nyong’o, Forrest Whitaker, Michael B. Jordan, Danai Gurira and Angela Bassett. It earned seven Oscar nominations, including best picture, the first superhero movie to do so. The film won three Oscars, including best costume design, best production design and best original score.
	

	“Black Panther: Wakanda Forever” grossed $859 million worldwide when it was released in 2022, and had one of the most profitable opening weekends post-pandemic, earning $331 million worldwide. The film was nominated for five Oscars, with Angela Bassett’s nomination for best supporting actress marking the first time any actor in a Marvel film was nominated for an Academy Award.

	Marvel fans won’t have to wait long to see Wright back in action as Black Panther, as she’s part of the sprawling “Avengers: Doomsday” cast. The film will hit theaters on Dec. 18.

schema.headline: ‘Black Panther 3’: David Jonsson to Play T’Challa’s Son as December 2028 Release Date Set

title: Winston Duke Trusts David Jonsson to Take On ‘Black Panther’: ‘I Think It’s Going to Be Great’
description:
Winston Duke is officially returning to Wakanda for “Black Panther 3”, and David Jonsson is coming along with him.

	Marvel teased the third “Black
body:
Winston Duke is officially returning to Wakanda for “Black Panther 3”, and David Jonsson is coming along with him.

	Marvel teased the third “Black Panther” at San Diego Comic-Con, which releases Dec. 15, 2028. Jonsson will play T’Challa’s son, Prince T’Challa II, continuing the late Chadwick Boseman’s legacy.

	“I trust him as an artist. I also trust the people who chose him,” Winston told Variety’s Angelique Jackson about Jonsson joining the franchise. “I trust Ryan [Coogler]. I trust the entire MCU executive team. I think it’s going to be great.”
	

	“Black Panther” was Duke’s first film, and he said he hopes to create a similarly welcoming experience for Jonsson. “How I was greeted and received into this world – which was with a lot of grace, being told it’s a safe space to work, to play — that’s what I wanted to extend to him,” he said. “I don’t have any advice. I know what I have to do with him, which is to play with him. I have to trust him. I have to give him the same grace that was extended to me.”

	Ryan Coogler will return to direct the film following “Black Panther: Wakanda Forever,” with Leticia Wright reprising her role as Shuri.

	Winston will also appear as M’Baku in the highly anticipated “Avengers: Doomsday,” which premieres Dec. 18. The film’s trailer has been viewed 503 million times since being released on Monday.

	“What I know is that we have their attention,” Winston said when asked about fans’ interest in the future of the MCU. “I think we have their attention because of so much trust that they have for the MCU. We’ve created and delivered so many movies over the years, and it’s never about any one director. It’s about the cohort.”
	

	The first “Black Panther” film released in 2018 and earned $1.3 billion at the worldwide box office, also receiving seven Oscar nominations and three wins.

schema.headline: Winston Duke Trusts David Jonsson to Take On ‘Black Panther’: ‘I Think It’s Going to Be Great’

title: Box Office: ‘The Odyssey’ Sails to $87 Million in Massive Second Weekend
description: “The Odyssey” continued its epic box office journey, scoring a sensational $87 million from 3,943 North American theaters in its second weekend of r
body:
“The Odyssey” continued its epic box office journey, scoring a sensational $87 million from 3,943 North American theaters in its second weekend of release. That’s a tally that most films, especially of the R-rated variety, would be happy to earn in their opening weekends.

	Ticket sales for “The Odyssey” declined just 30% from its sizable $123.5 million debut, a testament to the box office durability of director Christopher Nolan. Most tentpoles that open above $100 million would decline by 50% or more in subsequent weekends. Plus, R ratings can limit a film’s audience because they prevent most people under 18 from buying a ticket. To that end, the turnout for “The Odyssey” represents the second-biggest sophomore outing for an R-rated movie after Disney’s “Deadpool & Wolverine,” which earned $96 million in its second weekend after launching to a record-setting $221 million domestically. 
	

	After two weekends in theaters, Nolan’s big-budget adaptation of Homer’s epic poem, starring Matt Damon as the Greek king Odysseus, has grossed $286.4 million in North America and $639.6 million globally. “The Odyssey” will be tested next weekend with the release of “Spider-Man: Brand New Day.” Sony’s Marvel adventure, starring Tom Holland and Zendaya, could distract audiences. However, exhibitors are positively euphoric about the prospect of two massively popular movies to propel the typically slow month of August. 


	“Once or twice a year a movie opens big and then plays for weeks and weeks,” says David A. Gross, who publishes the box office newsletter FranchiseRe. “‘The Odyssey’ is showing that kind of holding power.”
	

	“The Odyssey” has been a force in Imax, which makes sense because it’s the first feature shot entirely with the company’s high-tech cameras. (Since Imax cameras are loud, cumbersome and expensive, most movies are shot digitally and utilize Imax only for certain action sequences.) So far “The Odyssey” has generated $140 million globally in Imax, including $78 million domestically and $62 million internationally. Imax’s coveted 70mm screens — of which there are only 41 in the world — contributed $5.2 million over the weekend and $16.9 million to date, representing 12.1% of the total Imax box office. Since cinephiles know that Imax 70mm is Nolan’s preferred format, most of those showtimes are sold out into September. 

	“’The Odyssey’ has crossed over from hit blockbuster to global cultural event,” says Imax’s CEO Richard Gelfond. “Our results indicate that audiences around the world will line up to experience this one-of-a-kind film in Imax for weeks, if not months, to come.”

	With euphoric word-of-mouth and outsized interest in premium large formats, “The Odyssey” is expected to remain a major draw throughout the summer and into the fall. It’ll wind up among the highest-grossing releases of the year. That prospect, along with the promise of Oscar nominations and the bragging rights of working with Nolan, the most bankable director of his generation, will easily justify the film’s price tag for Universal. The studio spent a staggering $250 million to produce and around $125 million to promote the movie.

	“The Odyssey” wasn’t the only movie inspired by Greek mythology to land among the top five at the weekend box office. “Hadestown: The Musical,” a filmed version of the very successful Broadway show, had a strong debut with $9.6 million from 1,949 theaters. To compare, a theatrical version of “Hamilton” earned $10.1 million from 1,825 screens while Broadway live-captures of favorites like “Waitress: The Musical” and “Merrily We Roll Along” opened to $2.6 million and $1.3 million, respectively. 

	“Hadestown,” a folk-operatic retelling of the Greek myth of Orpheus, a musician who ventures to the underworld to rescue his fiancée, Eurydice, was supposed to play in theaters for just five days. Given the positive reviews and popular demand, though, Crosswalk and LD Entertainment — which released “Hadestown” with Bleecker Street — are extending the run with plans to add additional dates and showtimes.
	

	Disney’s “Moana” and “Toy Story 5” captured second and third place on box office charts. “Moana” earned 10.5 million from 4,015 locations in its third weekend, a modest 40% decline. So far, the live-action version of the studio’s animated adventure has generated $102.5 million in North America and $228.2 million worldwide. Disney spent $250 million to reimagine the oceanic-set movie, so “Moana” will struggle to swim to profitability in its theatrical run.

	“Moana” might not inspire a live-action sequel, but Disney has plenty to celebrate now that “Toy Story 5” is the highest-grossing movie of the year with $1.022 billion globally. The animated fivequel added $10 million from 3,375 domestic theaters in its sixth outing, a mere 27% decline from the prior weekend. With grosses at $448.6 million in North America and $573.5 million internationally, “Toy Story 5” is poised to notch another box office benchmark. It’ll soon overtake its predecessor, 2019’s “Toy Story 4” ($1.07 billion), as the biggest installment in the beloved Pixar franchise. 

	Universal and Illumination’s “Minions and Monsters” tied with “Hadestown” for the No. 4 spot at the domestic box office. “Minions and Monsters” also brought in $9.6 million over the weekend, boosting its domestic tally to $155 million after four weekends on the big screen. The animated prequel has earned $411 million globally, which is significant against its $85 million budget. However, recent entries in the “Despicable Me” franchise have neared or surpassed the billion-dollar mark with ease, meaning the newest “Minions” may end up as the lowest-grossing in the series. Given the diminishing returns, Universal and Illumination, which have cranked out a new “Despicable Me” adventure about every two years since the original 2010 film, may want to wait a bit before Gru and his highlighter-yellow underlings return to theaters. 

	More to come…

title: PBS SoCal, KMEX Lead L.A. Local Emmy Wins; KVEA, KABC Land Top Newscast Prizes
description: PBS SoCal (KOCE and KCET) was the big winner Saturday night at the L.A. Area Emmy Awards, landing eight — including for live events-programming, ent
body:
PBS SoCal (KOCE and KCET) was the big winner Saturday night at the L.A. Area Emmy Awards, landing eight — including for live events-programming, entertainment, crime/social issues and arts. Univision’s KMEX was next, with seven, followed by Telemundo’s KVEA with six.

	KVEA once again won the newscast Emmys for daily daytime (11 a.m. to 7 p.m.) and daily evening (7 p.m. to 12 a.m.). Last year, KVEA won all three — also picking up daily morning (4 a.m. to 11 a.m.). But this year, KABC/ABC7 won that morning newscast Emmy.
	

	The 2026 Los Angeles Area Emmy Awards were held Saturday at the Skirball Cultural Center in Los Angeles, hosted by KABC entertainment reporter George Pennacchio. KABC’s David Ono received the 2026 Los Angeles Area Emmy Governors Award, “recognizing his more than three decades of broadcasting and his passion for in-depth storytelling.” Ono’s KABC co-anchor, Jovana Lara, presented him the honor.


	Bob Bain and Bob Bain Productions produced the ceremony, while Greg Taylor and Brian DeCloux are the Los Angeles Area Governors. Categories included Live and Breaking News Coverage, Crime and Social Issues, Culture and History, the Arts, Health and Science, Human Interest, Music, Sports and the Environment.

	Beyond PBS SoCal, KMEX and KVEA, other outlet winners included KABC/ABC7 (four), KNBC/NBC4 (four), Spectrum News 1 (two), Spectrum SportsNet (two), LA36 (one), Spectrum SportsNet LA (one) and USC football (one). 

	As for this year’s nominee totals, PBS SoCal landed 29 nominations; KABC/ABC7 received 21, Univision outlet KMEX received 20, Telemundo’s KVEA had 18, KNBC/NBC4 landed 15 and Spectrum News 1 had 10.
	

	For the station newscast awards, every TV station that submits is eligible. This year’s eligibility period was for the 2025 calendar year, which means many of the news categories winners focused on the devastating wildfires that ripped through the region last January.

title: One Killed, 16 Injured After Alleged Terrorist Plows Into Crowd at LGBTQ+ Parade in Germany
description:
Berlin Terror Attack
                          Maniac Allegedly Mows Down 17 People At Pride Para
body:
Berlin Terror Attack
                          Maniac Allegedly Mows Down 17 People At Pride Parade ...
                          Suspect ID'd, Still At Large
                      
                  
                                                                        Published 
                              July 26, 2026
                            5:56 AM PDT
                                                                      |
                                                                Updated 
                                  July 26, 2026
                                7:05 AM PDT
                                    
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                                  
      
    
            One person was killed and 16 others were injured Saturday when an alleged terrorist intentionally mowed down a crowd of revelers at a LGBTQ+ parade in Berlin, Germany, according to police.
      
    
            Cops said the tragedy occurred when a car barreled into Tiergarten -- Berlin's most prominent park -- plowing into a bunch of people near the route of the pride celebration. An army of police then responded and searched for the suspect, but he had already fled and is still at large. 
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Berlin Police say they have identified the alleged perpetrator as 21-year-old Abdul Ballout -- who allegedly has ties to an Islamic extremist group. A police spokesperson also said some of the victims had suffered life-threatening injuries ... and some had stab wounds.
      

      
      UPDATE: At least 1 dead, 15 injured after driver drove vehicle into crowd at CSD Pride Parade in Berlin, Germany. - DTS News Agency pic.twitter.com/bBpbWYRuix
              @AZ_Intel_
          
  
    
            Firefighters and paramedics provided medical aid to the victims. Photos show ambulances and first responders on scene after the parade was cancelled.
      
    
                  
          
                          
                
                  
      
    
            Berlin Mayor Kai Wegner issued a statement ... saying that "following a peaceful and vibrant pride parade, the rally for a tolerant and peaceful Berlin was attacked in the most brutal manner." Wegner added, "This is an attack on our free and cosmopolitan society."
      
    
            Hundreds of thousands of people had attended Berlin's Pride parade, which is one of Europe's largest LGBTQ+ celebrations.
